proverbs.igbo: Ilu bụ mmanụ ndị Igbo ji eri okwu.
proverbs.en: Proverb is the oil with which Igbo words are eaten.
proverbs.meaning: Proverbs make speech go down well. They give weight and grace to what is said, the way oil helps food along.
proverbs.usage: Said about proverbs themselves, to praise someone who speaks well or to open a talk that will use them.

proverbs.igbo: E were ilu ilu bie okwu, ofeke agbara aka laa
proverbs.en: When discussions are concluded in proverbs, the good-for-nothing goes home empty handed
proverbs.meaning: When elders settle a matter in proverbs, someone who never learned the deeper language leaves with nothing.
proverbs.usage: Encouraging a young person to learn proverbs, or remarking that much was said indirectly at a meeting.

proverbs.igbo: Onye gbara nkịtị kwere ekwe.
proverbs.en: One who kept quiet is in agreement.
proverbs.meaning: Silence is taken as agreement.
proverbs.usage: At a meeting, before a decision, to invite anyone who disagrees to speak now.

proverbs.igbo: Onye ụkọ anaghị atụ ilu.
proverbs.en: A messenger does not speak in proverbs.
proverbs.meaning: A messenger delivers the message plainly, as it was given, without adding to it.
proverbs.usage: Reminding someone sent with a message to say it straight. Its status as a proverb is pending review.

proverbs.igbo: Agwọ ofu onye hụrụ na-aghọ ya eke.
proverbs.en: A snake seen by one person alone seems like a python to him.
proverbs.meaning: A story with only one witness grows in the telling.
proverbs.usage: When a single person's account sounds larger than life, or to say why witnesses matter.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụ íché ha ka ényí ka ana ama enyi
proverbs.en: It is a stone the size of an elephant that you throw at an elephant
proverbs.meaning: Match your effort to the size of the task.
proverbs.usage: Before a big undertaking, to say that small measures will not do.

proverbs.igbo: Ejide ibe ji na aka, asaa agụụ okwu
proverbs.en: When you have a piece of yam in your hands, you can then reply hunger
proverbs.meaning: With something in hand, you can face a difficulty calmly.
proverbs.usage: On being prepared before trouble comes.

proverbs.igbo: Ọbụ ike na ume ka eji afụ opi
proverbs.en: It takes strength to blow a flute
proverbs.meaning: Every achievement takes strength and breath; nothing worthwhile is effortless.
proverbs.usage: Encouragement before hard work, or praise for work that clearly took effort.

proverbs.igbo: Ejighi ugegbe ele ihe agba na aka
proverbs.en: A mirror is not used to look at what is worn on the hand
proverbs.meaning: What is plain to see needs no proof.
proverbs.usage: When someone asks for evidence of something obvious.

proverbs.igbo: Awọ anaghị agba ọsọ ehihie n'efu.
proverbs.en: The toad does not run in the day time for nothing.
proverbs.meaning: Unusual behaviour has a cause. When something out of the ordinary happens, there is a reason behind it.
proverbs.usage: When someone acts out of character, to say it is worth asking why.

proverbs.igbo: Nkịta anaghị ata ọkpụkpụ a nyawara ya n'olu.
proverbs.en: The dog does not eat the bone hung on its neck.
proverbs.meaning: What is placed in your care, in plain view, is not yours to consume.
proverbs.usage: Reminding someone that what they were trusted with is not theirs to use up.

proverbs.igbo: Onye njenje na-aka onye isi awọ ama ihe.
proverbs.en: A traveler is more experienced than an elder.
proverbs.meaning: Travel teaches. Someone who has seen the world can know more than an elder who never left home.
proverbs.usage: Encouraging a young person to travel, or respecting what a traveller brings back.

proverbs.igbo: Mgbe nne amụbeghị ọchịagha ọkwa ndị ọgụ na agarị?
proverbs.en: When the warlord was not yet born, people still went to wars, didn't they?
proverbs.meaning: Life went on before you, and it can go on without you. No one is indispensable.
proverbs.usage: Gently humbling someone who acts as if nothing can happen without them.

proverbs.igbo: Mgbe ụtaba apụtebee o nwere onye azụzụ gburu?
proverbs.en: When the snuff had not yet existed, did catarrh kill anyone?
proverbs.meaning: People managed before this thing existed, so it is not as essential as it seems.
proverbs.usage: When someone claims they cannot do without something new.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụghị ebe aka ewu zọrọ ka ụkwụ ya na azọ
proverbs.en: A walking goat's fore and hindlimbs do not step on the same spots

proverbs.igbo: Agaghị ejikwa na ịsị ọkụkọ epeka nwere sị na ya na ewu bụ ọgbọ
proverbs.en: You can't say that because a fowl's head is small, that it is same mate with goat

proverbs.igbo: Onye buru chi ya uzo, o gbagbue onwe ya n'oso
proverbs.en: He who goes ahead of his 'chi', would run to death
proverbs.meaning: Don't rush ahead of your chi (your guardian spirit, your destiny). Pushing past your time ends badly.
proverbs.usage: Counselling patience to someone in too much of a hurry.

proverbs.igbo: Ebe onye dara ka chi ya kwaturu ya
proverbs.en: Where a person falls, is where his god pushed him down.
proverbs.meaning: Where a person falls is where their chi let them fall; a setback can be part of a larger path.
proverbs.usage: Reflecting on a misfortune without heaping blame on the one it happened to.

proverbs.igbo: A naghị eji ụtụtụ ama njọ ahia
proverbs.en: You don't know a bad sales day from the morning
proverbs.meaning: Don't judge the day by its morning. A slow start says little about how things will end.
proverbs.usage: Encouraging a trader, or anyone whose day or venture has started slowly.

proverbs.igbo: Ana achụ mbekwu n'ị́ké, ọ ga èfé elu?
proverbs.en: Does one pursue the tortoise with great speed? Is it going to fly?
proverbs.meaning: There is no need to rush after something that cannot escape.
proverbs.usage: Telling someone to calm down and take their time.

seeAlso.title: Mbe and the feast in the sky

proverbs.igbo: Ebule laa azụ, ọ bịa ọgụ.
proverbs.en: When the ram moves backwards, it comes for a fight.
proverbs.meaning: A step back can be a gathering of strength.
proverbs.usage: When someone withdraws for a while. Don't mistake it for giving up.

proverbs.igbo: Onye wetara ọjị wetara ndụ
proverbs.en: He who brings kola brings life
proverbs.meaning: Bringing kola is bringing goodwill; the one who offers it offers life and blessing.
proverbs.usage: Said when kola is presented to guests, as part of the welcome.

proverbs.igbo: Akanri kwọọ akaekpe, aka ekpe akwọọ aka nri
proverbs.en: When the right hand washes the left, the left reciprocates the gesture
proverbs.meaning: Help goes both ways. When you help others, they help you in turn.
proverbs.usage: Encouraging cooperation within a family, between neighbours or partners.

proverbs.igbo: Ewu mmadụ abụọ na enye nri na anwụ na agụụ
proverbs.en: A goat which is fed by two persons dies of hunger.
proverbs.meaning: When a duty belongs to two people loosely, each assumes the other did it, and the job is left undone.
proverbs.usage: When a task has no clear owner.

proverbs.igbo: Ewu ọha nwe na-anwụ n'agụrụ.
proverbs.en: A goat owned by the public die of hunger.
proverbs.meaning: What belongs to everyone is looked after by no one.
proverbs.usage: About shared property or shared work that everyone neglects.

proverbs.igbo: Ofu onye nwe okeọkpa mana ọha nwe olu ya
proverbs.en: One person owns the cock, but the public owns its crowing
proverbs.meaning: What one person owns can still benefit everyone.
proverbs.usage: When a private gift, talent or possession serves the whole community.

proverbs.igbo: Ọbụ oke ịgba iche iche mere na agwọ enweghị ụmụnna
proverbs.en: Too much individualism is the reason the snake has no kins men
proverbs.meaning: Going it alone leaves you without people to stand with you.
proverbs.usage: Calling a family or group to unity.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụ mmiri na enyere ncha aka ka o nwee gbaa ụfụfụ
proverbs.en: Water assists in bring out lather from soap
proverbs.meaning: Success comes with help from others.
proverbs.usage: Acknowledging the people whose help made something work.

proverbs.igbo: Ọyịm agwaram gị agwa bụ ezigbo ọyị. Akaaram agwa gị agwa bụ ajọ ọyị
proverbs.en: "My friend I told you" Is a good friend. "I would have told you" is a bad friend.
proverbs.meaning: A true friend warns you in time; a friend who speaks only after the fact is no friend.
proverbs.usage: About honest friendship, or after a warning that came too late.

proverbs.igbo: A na-esi n'ulọ mara mma pụọ ama
proverbs.en: Charity begins at home
proverbs.meaning: Good conduct starts at home before it is shown outside.
proverbs.usage: Reminding someone to begin with their own household.
proverbs.literalNote: The dataset gives an English equivalent ("Charity begins at home"); a literal rendering is pending review.

proverbs.igbo: Anụ gbaa ajọ ọsọ, a gbaa ya ajọ egbe.
proverbs.en: An animal that runs wickedly will be shot wickedly.
proverbs.meaning: Extreme behaviour invites an equally strong response.
proverbs.usage: A warning to someone acting recklessly that the reply will match.

proverbs.igbo: Mbe na mbe gaa ahịa, uru anaghị adị ya
proverbs.en: When two tortoises transact a business, both of them lose
proverbs.meaning: When two tricksters deal with each other, neither gains.
proverbs.usage: About two cunning people trying to outwit each other.

proverbs.igbo: Oji enyi nwee kwee ọya kedụzị anụ ọzọ ọ chọrọ ịmata
proverbs.en: After catching an elephant, which other animal do you want to catch?
proverbs.meaning: After the greatest success, be content.
proverbs.usage: Against greed, when someone who has done very well still wants more.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkụkọ nwa ogbenye bụ ehi ya
proverbs.en: A poor person's chicken is his cow
proverbs.meaning: Value is relative to what a person has. Respect what others hold dear, however small.
proverbs.usage: When someone belittles another's modest gift or possession.

proverbs.igbo: Onye kwụrụ ọtọ emegharịgị ahụ, ngwere arịgoro ya elu
proverbs.en: If one stands up without shaking his body, lizards will climb up his body.
proverbs.meaning: If you never stir to defend yourself, others will take advantage.
proverbs.usage: Encouraging someone to stand up for themselves.

proverbs.igbo: Ike adịghị ọkwụrụ gbaa mgbọrọgwụ, ọ sị na àlà esika ike
proverbs.en: If the okro that grew roots isn't strong, it will be like the ground is too strong.
proverbs.meaning: The weak blame their circumstances.
proverbs.usage: When someone blames others for their own lack of effort.

proverbs.igbo: I kpara akwụ kpara akwụ onye nwe akwụ eburukwa akwụ ya
proverbs.en: When you harvest palm fruits again and again, the owner of the palm fruits will carry his palm fruits.
proverbs.meaning: Taking what isn't yours, again and again, ends when the owner comes.
proverbs.usage: A warning to someone who keeps helping themselves to what belongs to another.

proverbs.igbo: Ụsakụụsa rie ogwumagana ọ kwụsị iri anụ.
proverbs.en: When the glutton eats a chameleon, he would stop eating meat.
proverbs.meaning: Greed eventually teaches its own lesson.
proverbs.usage: About someone whose excess finally caught up with them.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkụkọ mmanya na egbu hụ égbé ara na agba, isi ajụọ ya oyi
proverbs.en: When a drunk fowl meets a crazy kite, he calms down
proverbs.meaning: A troublemaker calms down on meeting someone wilder.
proverbs.usage: When a bully meets their match.

proverbs.igbo: Osisi kwu n'ụzọ na-ebu apa mma.
proverbs.en: A tree by the roadside always have machete scars.
proverbs.meaning: Whoever stands in a public place bears the marks of it.
proverbs.usage: Comforting someone in public life who is being criticised.

proverbs.igbo: Okenye anaghị anọ n'ụlọ ewu amụọ n'ọgbụ.
proverbs.en: An elder will not be at home while a goat gives birth in its tedder.
proverbs.meaning: An elder present is expected to step in; responsibility comes with age.
proverbs.usage: Reminding an elder, or anyone in charge, to act when something goes wrong on their watch.

proverbs.igbo: Agadi nwaanyi anaghị aka nka n'egwu o ma-agba
proverbs.en: An old woman does not get too old for a music she knows how to dance
proverbs.meaning: You never grow too old for what you know well.
proverbs.usage: Praising an elder who still does something with skill.

proverbs.igbo: Ogologo abụghị na nwam etola
proverbs.en: Growing tall does not mean that my child has grown up
proverbs.meaning: Size is not maturity.
proverbs.usage: To a young person who acts grown because they are tall.

proverbs.igbo: Akwụnye anụ n'ọkụ, nwata ejee ozi ezibeghị ya ezi
proverbs.en: When they place a piece of meat on the fire, a child goes on an errand he has not yet been sent
proverbs.meaning: Eagerness appears when there is something to gain.
proverbs.usage: Gentle teasing of helpfulness that comes just as the food is ready.

proverbs.igbo: Onye a na-abara mba bụ onye a hụrụ n'anya.
proverbs.en: One who is scolded is one who is loved.
proverbs.meaning: Correction is a sign of love.
proverbs.usage: To a child, or anyone, who feels they are scolded too often.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata na-eyighị nne na nna ya, kedụ onye ọ ga-eyi?
proverbs.en: A child that does not look like his parents, who will he look like?
proverbs.meaning: Children take after their parents.
proverbs.usage: When a child's ways mirror their parents', for good or ill.

proverbs.igbo: Okeọkpa kata ahụ, ọ kwawa akwa.
proverbs.en: When the cock matures, it begins to crow.
proverbs.meaning: When one comes of age, one's voice is heard.
proverbs.usage: Of a young person stepping into responsibility.

proverbs.igbo: Ejighi okwute elele isi kara aka
proverbs.en: They don't use stones to check for mature heads.

proverbs.igbo: Ihe ana ahụghị na afọ nne ewi ekwesịghị ka ahụ ya na nke nwa ya
proverbs.en: Whatever wasn't seen in the stomach of a mother hare should not be seen in that of the child.
